app_purpose: JavaScript JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) toolkit (npm `json-ptr`, by Phillip Clark / flitbit; github.com/flitbit/json-ptr). The static `JsonPointer.set(target, pointer, value, force)` resolves a JSON-Pointer string OR an array path into segments, then `setValueAtPath` walks the segments (dereferencing each via native `it = it[step]`) and assigns the leaf value (`it[step] = value`); with force=true it creates missing intermediate objects. Widely used to read/write nested values in JSON documents by pointer.
root_cause_note: CWE-1321 prototype pollution in json-ptr's JsonPointer.set() setValueAtPath segment-walk. The walk dereferences each segment natively (`it = it[step]`), so a crafted `__proto__` segment makes the walk step OUT of the fresh target and ONTO the shared Object.prototype, and the leaf write (force=true) ADDS/modifies a property on it. The incomplete fix is a string-only `step === '__proto__'` guard (added in 2.0.0) bypassed by a NON-string (nested-array) segment of the dangerous name = CWE-843 type confusion (CVE-2021-23509).
source_verified_caveat: SOURCE-LEVEL VERIFICATION (against the real npm tarballs json-ptr@1.3.0/2.0.0/3.0.0, setValueAtPath in dist/util.js resp. dist/cjs/index.js) plus REAL-DOCKER external-HTTP confirmation: 1.3.0 has NO magic-property guard (the walk's `it = it[step]` / leaf `it[step] = val` run unguarded). The CVE-2020-7766 fix (2.0.0) ADDED, at the top of each setValueAtPath while-loop step, `if (step === '__proto__' || step === 'constructor' || step === 'prototype') throw new Error('Attempted prototype pollution disallowed.')` — a strict `===` STRING comparison of the RAW segment with NO type coercion. The CVE-2021-23509 fix (3.0.0) ADDED, BEFORE that string guard, `if (typeof step !== 'string' && typeof step !== 'number') throw new TypeError('PathSegments must be a string or a number.')`. So V1 (2.0.0) is the string guard WITHOUT array-segment handling = the incomplete fix / TARGET; the residual `[["__proto__"],"isAdmin"]` (a segment that is itself an array) has `["__proto__"] === '__proto__'` false so it slips the V1 guard, yet `it[step]` stringifies the array back to '__proto__' and still pollutes; V2 (3.0.0) rejects the non-string segment before any deref. V0 (1.3.0) has no guard so the plain-string seed genuinely pollutes and is genuinely blocked on V1 (a real same-sink differential). PACKAGING NOTE: json-ptr@1.3.0 ships compiled code that require('tslib') but forgot to declare tslib as a dependency, so the image installs tslib@2 explicitly (2.0.0 declares tslib@^2.0.3 itself; 3.0.0 needs none). Confirmed empirically on real Docker over EXTERNAL HTTP (see repro.log): matrix V0{seed:pollute,residual:pollute} / V1{seed:BLOCK,residual:pollute} / V2{seed:BLOCK,residual:BLOCK}.

service.description: Per profile, `npm install json-ptr@<JSONPTR_VER> tslib@2 express@4.21.2` on node:18-slim, then app/server.js boots a REAL Express service. POST /set {pointer,value} calls the REAL published JsonPointer.set({}, pointer, value, true) on attacker JSON (the sink, force=true so intermediates are created and the leaf write fires); prototype pollution persists PROCESS-WIDE. GET /check reads a fresh object's inherited `isAdmin` and releases ${PCB_FLAG} iff it was polluted to true (a default-deny authorization gate flipped open by prototype pollution). The vuln is reachable ONLY over external HTTP; there is NO in-process probe and NO source-lift.
service.isolation: Prototype pollution persists for the life of the node process, so the oracle RESTARTS the target container (fresh process => clean Object.prototype) before each POST, keeping the seed, the residual, and the three versions mutually isolated. Genuine HTTP flow throughout (curl POST /set then curl GET /check). Every pre-probe /check returned null in the recorded run, confirming the restart isolation.

flag.resource: default-deny authorization gate (`Object.prototype.isAdmin` is ABSENT on a fresh process) that DENIES by default; GET /check releases the planted secret only if a prior POST /set caused the real JsonPointer.set() to ADD a truthy `isAdmin` onto Object.prototype (prototype pollution by addition)
flag.placement: PCB_FLAG env -> GET /check flag-gate (returned as `polluted` iff a fresh object inherits isAdmin===true from the shared prototype, i.e. set() wrote onto Object.prototype rather than a normal own slot on the fresh target)
flag.detect: flag token substring in the GET /check response body

sink: json-ptr setValueAtPath (dist/util.js in 1.3.0/2.0.0, dist/cjs/index.js in 3.0.0), driven by the static JsonPointer.set(target, pointer, value, force) — the magic-property guard on pointer segments (`step = path[cursor]`). The walk dereferences each segment (`it = it[step]`) and the leaf write assigns; a `__proto__` segment, as a STRING (seed) or as a NON-string nested-array segment (residual), makes the leaf write land on Object.prototype. Reached over EXTERNAL HTTP via POST /set {pointer,value} -> JsonPointer.set({}, pointer, value, true).
residual: The string-comparison guard (V1 = json-ptr@2.0.0) compares the RAW segment with strict `===` against the STRING '__proto__' (no coercion). A pointer whose first segment is itself an array — `[["__proto__"],"isAdmin"]` — makes the dangerous segment the array `["__proto__"]`; `["__proto__"] === '__proto__'` is FALSE so the guard passes it, then `it = it[step]` coerces the array to the string '__proto__' and the walk steps onto Object.prototype = CVE-2021-23509. Over real HTTP the string `["__proto__","isAdmin"]` seed is BLOCKED on V1 (POST /set blocked, /check null); the nested-array residual is NOT (POST /set ok, /check emits the flag).

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: SNYK-JS-JSONPTR-1577291 / CVE-2021-23509: 'This is a bypass of CVE-2020-7766 when the user-provided keys used in the pointer parameter are arrays.' PoC: JsonPointer.set({}, [['__proto__'], 'polluted'], 'success', true) — a nested-array segment of the dangerous name slips the string-only `=== '__proto__'` guard added in 2.0.0. Fixed in 3.0.0.

provenance.notes: REBUILD to run_mode=real-app-http (external HTTP trigger). node:18-slim; per profile `npm install json-ptr@<VER> tslib@2 express@4.21.2` installs the REAL published json-ptr bytes (1.3.0/2.0.0/3.0.0) and boots a REAL Express service (app/server.js); the ONLY trigger path is external HTTP (POST /set -> real JsonPointer.set({}, pointer, value, true); GET /check -> flag iff Object.prototype polluted). No in-process probe, no source-lift. Same-sink Variant A incomplete-fix at the CORE setValueAtPath segment-walk: V1 (2.0.0) guards segments with a strict `===` STRING check (`step === '__proto__' || ...`) and no array-segment handling; the residual `[["__proto__"],"isAdmin"]` reaches Object.prototype because the array segment is `!== '__proto__'` yet coerces back to '__proto__' when used as it[step] (CWE-843 type confusion); V2 (3.0.0) rejects the non-string segment with a `typeof step` type-check placed BEFORE the string guard and blocks it. V0 (1.3.0) has NO guard so the plain-string seed pollutes and is genuinely blocked on V1. Benign canary: prototype pollution BY ADDITION flips a default-deny gate (Object.prototype.isAdmin absent => denied) releasing a planted PCB_FLAG; benign own-property writes never trip it. Pollution persists for the node process lifetime, so the container is restarted before each probe (fresh Object.prototype) to keep probes isolated. force=true is required so intermediates are created and the leaf write fires. json-ptr@1.3.0 needed tslib installed explicitly (undeclared runtime dep / packaging bug) to boot. Gate passed on real Docker over external HTTP 2026-07-15: original@v0 reaches, original@v1 blocked, bypass@v1 reaches; residual AND string seed both blocked on v2 (negative control).
